---
title: "Incremental cellular computation"
---

The native `execution::IncrementalInteractions<State, Output>` class evaluates
pure callbacks from a declared `geometry::dependency::ExplicitPattern` and
caches their results. A localized source update invalidates only interactions
that read that source. Parameter or context epoch changes invalidate the whole
cache. An explicit eligibility worklist determines which invalid results may
be recomputed now. This is reusable computation machinery; a consumer supplies
the biological interpretation, equations, event semantics, and scientific
validation.

## Dependency and cache contract

An immutable `geometry::dependency::ExplicitPattern` declares callback
**read dependencies**. Its stable edge IDs identify interactions; each
participant identifies a source by `(role, entity_id)`. Role is part of source
identity. A destination that is only written by the consumer does not need to
be a read dependency. Repeated participants remain repeated callback inputs,
even though the pattern's reverse postings deduplicate them for invalidation.
The pattern's structure epoch remains separate from source generations and
parameter/context epochs.

The cache is exact under these requirements:

- Every state read, including a state-dependent eligibility decision performed
  inside the callback, appears in the declared dependencies.
- Every changed source is submitted with a strictly increasing generation.
  Updates are explicit; the cache does not compare values or infer changes.
- The callback is pure. External parameter or context changes use a different
  `EvaluationEpochs` value. Time, random draws, hidden mutable state and external
  I/O are not implicit dependencies. A stochastic consumer must include its
  random state or explicit realization in declared inputs/context.
- `State` and `Output` behave as immutable values once published. Copying a
  pointer to mutable external storage does not make that storage immutable.

There is no built-in tolerance, hysteresis, approximate change suppression,
dtype conversion, or automatic numerical precision selection. Template types
make storage/output choices explicit; callback arithmetic determines multiply
and accumulation precision. A consumer introducing tolerance-based updates
owns the approximation and its validation.

`SourceReadSnapshot` records each input's role, stable entity ID, generation,
and immutable value in original participant order. Each cached record owns its
reads and output. Retaining a `cached(id).record` keeps an old evaluation
inspectable after subsequent steps. `result(id)` returns a reference valid
until its record is replaced; retain the record when a longer lifetime is
needed. `PreparedReadIndex`, exposed by `cache.incidence()`, builds a dense
source-key lookup over the pattern's existing postings; it does not duplicate
their ownership.

## State change, events, and publication

`step(updates, epochs)` recomputes all dirty interactions. Its optional
`ActiveWorklist` restricts eligibility. A null eligibility pointer means all
dirty work; an empty worklist means no work. `event_eligibility(event_sources)`
forms a worklist through the pattern's native reverse-posting query. A clean
interaction receiving an event remains cached; an event that changes the
callback's mathematical inputs must also update a source or context epoch.

Ineligible dirty interactions stay dirty across steps. `cached(id)` exposes
their last record together with `valid == false`; `result(id)` rejects stale or
absent output. Reopening eligibility eventually reevaluates the latest source
values. Consumers must not treat an old cached record as a current output.

The class stages source updates and all selected callback results before
publishing any of them. Invalid updates, allocation failures, or thrown
callbacks leave the previously committed sources, epochs, dirty work and
cached results intact. External callback side effects cannot be rolled back
and violate the purity requirement. The engine is single-owner host code;
concurrent mutation is unsupported.

Eligibility must retain the same immutable pattern object as the cache.
Changes to dependency structure require a new cache for the new snapshot;
cross-epoch cache migration and dependency discovery are not implemented.

## Native usage

```cpp
#include <Cellerator/geometry/dependency/explicit_pattern.hh>
#include <Cellerator/execution/dependency/incremental.hh>

#include <cassert>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <memory>
#include <vector>

namespace dep = cellerator::geometry::dependency;
namespace execution = cellerator::execution;

int main() {
    auto reads = std::make_shared<dep::ExplicitPattern>(
        std::vector<dep::PatternEdge>{
            {10, {{0,0,100}, {0,0,200}}},
            {20, {{0,0,200}, {0,0,300}}},
            {30, {{0,0,400}}}});

    execution::IncrementalInteractions<float,float> cache(reads,
        {{{0,0,100},0,1}, {{0,0,200},0,2},
         {{0,0,300},0,3}, {{0,0,400},0,4}},
        [](auto interaction_id, const auto& snapshot, auto epochs) {
            (void)interaction_id;
            (void)epochs;
            float total = 0;
            for (std::size_t i = 0; i < snapshot.size(); ++i)
                total += snapshot.at(i).value;
            return total;
        });

    const execution::PreparedReadIndex& index = cache.incidence();
    assert(index.source_ordinal({0,0,100}) == 0);
    auto initial = cache.step({}, {});
    assert((initial.evaluated_ids == std::vector<std::uint64_t>{10, 20, 30}));
    assert(cache.result(10) == 3 && cache.result(20) == 5 && cache.result(30) == 4);

    auto changed = cache.step({{{0,0,100},1,8}}, {});
    assert((changed.evaluated_ids == std::vector<std::uint64_t>{10}));
    assert(cache.result(10) == 10 && cache.result(20) == 5 && cache.result(30) == 4);

    auto no_events = cache.event_eligibility({});
    cache.step({{{0,0,200},1,7}}, {}, &no_events);
    assert(cache.pending_invalid() == 2);
    auto event = cache.event_eligibility({{0,0,100}});
    cache.step({}, {}, &event); // evaluates 10; 20 remains dirty
    assert(cache.result(10) == 15 && cache.pending_invalid() == 1);
    cache.step({}, {});            // evaluates 20 from latest sources
    assert(cache.result(20) == 10);
}
```

`PreparedReadIndex` handles source-to-interaction invalidation. For numerical
operations over values in a physical entity layout, `execution::PreparedIncidence`
supplies addresses and `ops::incidence` supplies gather, joint-reduce, and
scatter arithmetic. Those APIs solve a separate addressing-and-computation
problem; the callback cache does not require them.

The executable [native test](../tests/framework/native/incremental_test.cc)
uses an independent full-recompute loop to verify identical outputs after a
localized update while observing one callback instead of three. It also checks
repeated incidences, role identity, source snapshots, epoch invalidation,
eligibility, malformed updates and callback-failure rollback. Callback-count
reduction is not a measured elapsed-time speedup.

## CUDA changed-source frontier

`execution::PreparedReadIndex` exposes source keys and CSR offsets while
borrowing postings owned by `ExplicitPattern`. Its
`make_device_ordinal_projection()` explicitly creates dense interaction
ordinals for upload. Map changed keys with `source_ordinal`; never cast
biological entity IDs directly to dense slots. Retain the immutable pattern and
the projection buffer through device use.

`cellerator::modeling::cuda::build_changed_frontier` visits those
changed-source posting rows and
forms a compact, deduplicated interaction worklist. A warp processes a changed
source row; device-wide atomic claims handle duplicates across rows. It uses
no numerical arithmetic, dense all-pairs scan, allocation, device switch,
implicit synchronization or host status copy. Its output order is unspecified;
sort separately when a consumer requires stable edge order.

The declaration is in `<Cellerator/modeling/cuda/frontier.hh>` and its current
CUDA owner is `Cellerator::framework_cuda`. The host pattern and read index
remain available through `Cellerator::native_data` or `Cellerator::modeling`;
the frontier accepts explicit device buffers and does not synchronize or
publish host-cache state for the caller.

The borrowed device buffers, explicit CUDA stream, scratch capacity and output
capacity are part of the call. Scratch/status storage cannot be used
concurrently; sequential reuse on one stream is supported. Each call clears
one claim per interaction, so its work includes **O(number of interactions)**
scratch initialization plus changed rows and their postings. It is not a claim
of total cost proportional only to the active frontier. Host source preparation,
upload, allocation, output ordering and synchronization also belong in any
complete-path measurement.

The function returns launch or argument errors immediately. After stream
completion, `FrontierStatus.flags` reports invalid source indices, malformed
selected posting ranges/ordinals, or insufficient output capacity. On any flag,
`written` is zero and output storage must not be consumed. `required` reports
the exact union size when no input-content error occurred, including an
overflow-only result. Retry overflow with adequate capacity; do not execute a
partial frontier. Output storage may have been touched before a flag was set.

This primitive produces **invalidations**. A later eligibility decision must
preserve dirty interactions it excludes. The host cache and CUDA frontier are
composable primitives, not an automatically synchronized device cache: the
caller owns transfers and GPU callback dispatch.

## Validation boundary

The complete example above and the focused native check compiled with C++20,
`-Wall -Wextra -Werror`, against the current host owners. The installed
consumer interface remains `Cellerator::native_data` or its composing
`Cellerator::modeling` target; this source-tree command validates the test
contract directly:

```sh
g++ -std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -Iinclude \
  tests/framework/native/incremental_test.cc \
  src/containers/posting_index.cc \
  src/geometry/dependency/compact_support.cc \
  src/geometry/dependency/explicit_pattern.cc \
  src/geometry/dependency/posting_index.cc \
  src/execution/dependency/read_index.cc \
  src/execution/dependency/workset.cc \
  -o /tmp/cellerator-incremental-test
/tmp/cellerator-incremental-test
```

The CUDA frontier and its [smoke test](../tests/framework/cuda/frontier_smoke.cu)
compiled and linked with CUDA 12.9 for `sm_70`. The device test compares with a
set-union oracle across duplicate and empty rows, output-capacity boundaries,
and malformed source/posting cases. Focused V100 results and sanitizer outcomes
are in the [validation report](../planning/v100-framework-2026-10-29/REPORT.md).
Performance remains unmeasured. GPU execution must use the repository's
existing admitted execution route. The validation result above predates the
current C++20 minimum; the command below expresses the current compiler floor
and does not revise the source-bound historical result.

```sh
nvcc -std=c++20 -arch=sm_70 -Iinclude \
  tests/framework/cuda/frontier_smoke.cu src/modeling/cuda/frontier.cu \
  -o /tmp/cellerator-frontier-smoke
```

The scoped [implementation draft](incremental_cellular/draft.md) records the
design alternatives and consumed KDA/KernelWiki guidance. No biological
validity, generalized adaptive execution, or measured acceleration is implied.
